target_customer: E-commerce retailers and online brands that want to grow sales through customer referrals
problem: Online stores wanted word of mouth sales but lacked a tested way to design and measure referral offers after checkout.
business_model: SaaS with services; early model was a free base product plus fees tied to incremental sales

founders.name: Allan Grant
founders.role: CEO per TechCrunch 2013; CTO per YC page
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder in TechCrunch January 2012 and as co-founder and CEO in October 2011 and March 2013 articles; no other founders were named in the sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Cross-site testing of referral offers across about 700 partner sites and fraud handling needed real engineering, though the base web components were standard.

defensibility.rationale: Optimization data from many stores helps, but referral widgets were easy to imitate and rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge; Talkable remained private and independent as a referral platform with around 51 to 200 employees.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2011 said users got 30 to 60 percent of buying customers to share offers and reported sales lifts up to 15 percent; by March 2013 Curebit had about 3,000 clients including Bonobos, Restaurant.com and Jawbone.

branding.domain_note: Uses talkable.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional; tagline We're the Premium, Next-Generation Referral Platform, and We'll Prove It

rebrands.why: Not stated by the company; one commentary source dates it to 2015 and ties it to the word talkable, which is not verified

brand_strength.rationale: Talkable states the product idea in the name and the rename removed the opaque Curebit, but no sources show press on the brand, merch or community.

outcome_analysis: Curebit launched at the March 2011 demo day, raised a 1.2 million dollar seed in January 2012 and by March 2013 reached about 3,000 clients at break-even run rate while saying it was not raising a Series A. It later renamed itself Talkable and still operates privately with offices in San Francisco and London. The slow, mostly self funded path points to a durable niche business rather than a venture scale outcome.
notes: The YC page calls Allan Grant founder and CTO while TechCrunch calls him CEO. Founding year 2010 comes from a Retail Dive press release seen in a search snippet. Total raised of 4.2M appears only on Craft.co and was not recorded as a round because no rounds or dates were given. The CB Insights page returned 403. No Series A found; TechCrunch March 2013 says the company was not raising one. Competitor list is empty: the 2011 TechCrunch articles name no rivals (they compare it to Google Web Optimizer and Dropbox's referral program), and searches found Friendbuy and Extole only in later sources (Friendbuy seed dated 2010 on an aggregator, Extole 2013 TechCrunch), which are not dated close enough to the batch to list.
